title: Weather Watchers
subject: science
learningGoal: Observe and record weather using simple evidence: sky, wind and temperature feel.
realWorldHook: Weather forecasters start by observing carefully, just like scientists.

materials.item: A strip of paper or ribbon
materials.householdSubstitution: A tissue or a light leaf

materials.item: Paper and pencil for a weather chart

noPurchaseRoute: Use a strip of scrap paper as a wind streamer and draw the chart.
parentPreview: You go to a window, doorway or garden together, observe the sky, test the wind with a paper streamer, and record it on a simple chart.

parent.parentSays: Scientists observe the weather every day. What's it like outside right now?

child.screen: What's the weather like right now?
child.readAloudText: What's the weather like right now?

parent.parentSays: Head to a window or doorway together and ask what the sky looks like right now.
parent.whyThisWorks: Naming what you see is the first step of recording evidence.

child.screen: Look at the sky. What do you see?
child.readAloudText: Look at the sky. Is it sunny, cloudy or rainy?

parent.parentSays: Hold the paper streamer up. Does it hang down, wave a little, or fly straight out?

child.screen: Hold up your streamer. How is it moving?
child.readAloudText: Hold up your streamer. How is it moving?

parent.parentSays: Draw a symbol for the sky and wind on today's line of the chart.

child.screen: Draw today's weather on your chart.
child.readAloudText: Draw today's weather on your chart.

parent.parentSays: How did the streamer help us know about wind we can't see?

child.screen: How did the streamer show the wind?
child.readAloudText: How did the streamer show us the wind? Tell your grown-up.

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
What do you predict the weather will be tomorrow? Let's check!

expectedResponses: Sky and wind recorded with symbols
Explains the streamer shows wind moving it

misconceptions.signal: Says there is no wind because you can't see it.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: We can't see the wind itself. What can we see it doing?

misconceptions.signal: Thinks every cloud means rain right now.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Is it raining right now even though there are clouds?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: If the streamer flies straight out, what does that tell us?

interpretation.partial: Says something about the streamer moving.

child.screen: The streamer flies straight out. What's the weather?
child.readAloudText: The streamer flies straight out. Is it windy or still?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: How could we tell if it rained in the night without seeing it?

interpretation.clear: Suggests evidence: puddles, wet ground, a cup left outside.

child.screen: How could you tell it rained in the night?
child.readAloudText: How could you tell if it rained in the night? Tell your grown-up.

extension: Record the weather every day for a week, then tally: how many sunny days?

shorterVersion.description: Sky and wind only, observed from a window.

accessibilityAdaptations: Observe from a window if going outside is hard.
Use stickers or pictures for the chart.

hazards: Going outside near roads or water
safety.supervision: An adult goes outside with the child and stays close. Observe from a window or doorway if outside isn't safe.
stopConditions: The child goes near a road or water
It is very hot or very cold
safety.cleanup: Bring the streamer and chart inside.
